name: rms_ui
description: Web fleet / robot status UI at the site RMS IP. Primary site/operator surface for AGV alarms, roster/map, and overall fleet health; L1 may use the same overview remotely; L2/L3 use deeper RMS views plus WCS SQL/API corroboration. Not SSMS and not tipper WebVisu.

name: wcs_api
description: Logical catalog of OptiSweep System/AGV/Tote APIs. Executed via Apidog on primary or via Ignition for Aveva. Includes unplanned-restart host-service checklist.

name: site_interview
description: Remote FORTNA gathers observables the customer/client can see: stacklight color, E-stop depressed, tipper alarm text/photo, messages flowing, chute open/closed.

name: apidog
description: Locally hosted API client on WCS primary for System/AGV/Tote APIs. Same APIs Ignition uses to feed Aveva. Primary L2/L3 surface for GetAGVStatuses, closeout, exchange, zone config, etc.

name: operator
description: Customer/client site personnel (tipper/hospital/operator station) -- NOT a FORTNA support team member. Same side of the fence as 'customer' in Salesforce/RCA language. Performs on-site physical work (E-stop, LOTO, floor recovery), guided remotely by FORTNA L1/L2/L3; is the only role that performs a physical E-stop reset. FORTNA CSE may coach these actions but does not perform them as their own job.

name: L1_support
description: FORTNA Technical Support, remote (not on-site). Primary point of contact and Salesforce ticket owner; first-pass remote triage (RMS overview / AGV status, site report, coaching). Prefers support-safe, read-oriented surfaces. Does not perform SSMS/WCS DB deep dives, Ignition admin recovery, mutating APIs, or physical E-stop -- escalates to L2/L3 for deeper remote tooling.

name: L2_support
description: FORTNA Escalation Support, remote (not on-site). Technical investigation and resolution owner with deeper remote access than L1: RMS beyond overview, WCS API/Apidog, SSMS (read-only first), Event Viewer, Ignition gateway/OPC connections, Stunnel, tipper WebVisu heartbeat. Owns corroboration and restore paths beyond L1 authority, including RMS soft stop (pause) -- which is a software pause action, never a substitute for or synonym of a physical E-stop. Escalates to L4 when the incident or RCA cannot be handled independently.

name: L3_support
description: FORTNA Escalation Support, remote (not on-site) -- same remote posture and tooling depth as L2, with ownership of persistent/recurring issues and RCA production. Escalates to L4 (Software Development) when the incident or RCA cannot be resolved independently.

description: All location information shown as orange stations on RMS.

key_fields.name: StationNumber
key_fields.meaning: Station / workstation number for the location.

key_fields.name: Occupied
key_fields.meaning: Whether the location is currently occupied.

key_fields.name: Zone
key_fields.meaning: Zone associated with the location (sorter-side zones).

key_fields.name: LocationType
key_fields.meaning: Type of location (Sorter*, Tipper*, Hospital*, ShutDown*, GLD*).

key_fields.name: MaxAgvs
key_fields.meaning: Max number of AGVs allowed at that location.

key_fields.name: DwellTracking
key_fields.meaning: True/false whether dwell time should be tracked at this location.

key_fields.name: Coordinates (XY)
key_fields.meaning: X/Y coordinate fields for the location, described as lat/long-style coordinates (not enums), in centimeters. Cross-check the RMS orange-location workstation ID shown on the corresponding RMS station/segment against this model's station concept.

key_fields.name: Sequence
key_fields.meaning: Location's sequence number (used together with CellCode/LocationType for shutdown-staging and sorter-queue ordering).

key_fields.name: CellCode
key_fields.meaning: Cell/lattice code for the location (cross-references CellCodeDatabaseModel.CellCode and RobotDatabaseModel.CellCode).

key_fields.name: LastSent

name: SorterSideDatabaseModel
description: Defines sorter legs: entrance/exit queue locations, tipper count, disabled flag.

key_fields.name: TipperCount
key_fields.meaning: Number of tippers associated with the sorter side, used for round-robin assignment across the closest tippers (can vary by phase).

key_fields.name: Disabled
key_fields.meaning: Whether the sorter side is disabled. During phased site rollout, sorter sides not included in the current phase's CSV load are disabled by default; a phase-based database update script flips them enabled when that phase goes live. A sorter side reading Disabled during a phased cutover can therefore be expected configuration, not a fault.

name: SortLocationsDatabaseModel
description: Contains all the sorter locations and their respective queue locations. The queue location is the location behind the sorter location where the AGV with an empty tote will move to fill when an exchange happens. Also a zone/shutdown-queue-sequence -> station/location mapping lookup used to translate a shutdown queue sequence number tied to a zone into the target sorter station/location.

key_fields.name: SorterId
key_fields.meaning: The sorter (sort) location id — FK into RobotLocationDatabaseModel for the sorter-side location itself.

key_fields.name: StagingId
key_fields.meaning: Staging location id associated with this sort location (observed NULL in most sample rows; used for exchange staging).

key_fields.name: QueueId
key_fields.meaning: The queue location behind the sorter location where the AGV with an empty tote moves to and stages, so it can fill the sorter location during an exchange.

key_fields.name: Sequence
key_fields.meaning: Sequence ordering used as a lookup key together with zone to resolve the target station/location, and to order sort locations from the sorter entrance queue; sequence values 1–4 start from the sorter entrance queue, and compression (AGVs moving together to close gaps) preserves this order.

key_fields.name: SorterSideDatabaseModelId
key_fields.meaning: FK to the SorterSideDatabaseModel row identifying which sorter side these locations belong to.

name: CellCodeDatabaseModel
description: Stores all cell codes in the map. When a new AGV is added to the system while in a running state, the system first checks if the AGV's current cell code is in a missing zone under the sorter; if not, it uses this table to look up which hospital the cell code is connected to and sends an Initialize command to Geek.

key_fields.name: CellCode
key_fields.meaning: Cell/node code analogous to an RMS node code (vendor-agnostic).

key_fields.name: X
key_fields.meaning: X coordinate for the cell code.

key_fields.name: Y
key_fields.meaning: Y coordinate for the cell code.

key_fields.name: HospitalDatabaseModelId
key_fields.meaning: FK to the HospitalDatabaseModel this cell code is connected to — used when initializing an AGV whose current cell code is not in a missing zone under the sorter.

name: RobotDatabaseModel
description: Robot/AGV live state: contains the data for every robot in the system including its state, tote name, assigned sorter side, current/destination location, and state.

key_fields.name: State
key_fields.meaning: Robot state enum (Tipper/Hospital/Charger/Sorter/GLD/ShutDown family). Observed live values include SWaitingInzone, Removed, SWaitingForExchange, GoCharge, MovingToChargerEntranceQueue, MovingToTipperQueue.

key_fields.name: ToteId
key_fields.meaning: Tote currently associated with robot (labeled ToteId in the live query results; NULL when the robot has no tote).

key_fields.name: CommandId
key_fields.meaning: FK to the robot's current RobotCommandDatabaseModel row.

key_fields.name: ChargesSinceLastCharged
key_fields.meaning: Count of charge cycles since the robot was last fully charged.

key_fields.name: ChargeKick
key_fields.meaning: Whether the robot was kicked off the charger (relates to ChargingThresholdsDatabaseModel kick-off threshold).

key_fields.name: Status
key_fields.meaning: Status enum, observed values include NORMAL and REMOVED.

key_fields.name: ErrorCode
key_fields.meaning: Active AGV error code, e.g. 21085, 12003 (cross-references AgvErrorModel.Code).

key_fields.name: Coordinate
key_fields.meaning: Location label for the robot's coordinate reference (observed value "RoboticsModule.Messages.Location").

key_fields.name: CellCode
key_fields.meaning: Current cell/lattice code the robot is reporting (cross-references CellCodeDatabaseModel.CellCode).

key_fields.name: Angle
key_fields.meaning: Robot heading/angle at its current location.

key_fields.name: Current
key_fields.meaning: Live electrical current draw reported by the AGV.

key_fields.name: Voltage
key_fields.meaning: Live battery voltage reported by the AGV.

key_fields.name: IsToteEmpty
key_fields.meaning: Whether the tote currently on the robot is empty (1) or not (0).

key_fields.name: LastCommandGuid
key_fields.meaning: GUID of the last command sent to this robot (cross-references RobotCommandDatabaseModel).

name: LatticeCodeModel
description: Stores the lattice codes and their respective station IDs; when a tote is inducted or dropped off, Geek requires a lattice code for the location, and the Geek Comm module uses this table to convert the StationId from a robotics-module request into the lattice code Geek requires.

key_fields.name: StationId
key_fields.meaning: Respective station ID that maps to the lattice code.

key_fields.name: LatticeCode
key_fields.meaning: Lattice code Geek requires for induct/drop-off translation, e.g. 1005104001.

key_fields.name: HospitalStationId

Safety Signal Words and Symbols
description: Four safety signal words (DANGER, WARNING, CAUTION, NOTICE) and an electrical hazard symbol are used to alert operators to personal safety and equipment handling risks.

name: Operator Safety Responsibility
description: Operators must read and understand the manual before operating the conveyor. The user is solely responsible for complying with all applicable safety laws and site-specific standards.

name: Lift Connecting Rod Assembly Safety Warning
description: Approaching or extending a hand into the lifting connecting rod assembly while the robot is lifting can cause serious personal injury. Operators must ensure no one is near the assembly before starting the robot when powered on.

name: Robot Movement Trajectory Safety Warning
description: Personnel must be aware of the OptiSweep product's movement trajectory and must not interfere with its line of travel.

name: Tipper Contact Safety Warning

name: Operator Station Lockout/Tagout Procedure Reference

name: Visu_Dual_MCP HMI Screen Reference

description: The OptiSweep Operation and Maintenance Manual is organized into six chapters and appendices covering safety, system overview, operation, troubleshooting, maintenance, and spare parts.

name: OptiSweep Warranty Service Request Requirements
description: Warranty service requests for OptiSweep equipment require use of the Service Request Fax Sheet (Chapter 8) and attachment of the Maintenance Service History.

name: OptiSweep Manual Abbreviations and Acronyms
description: Defines abbreviations and acronyms used in the OptiSweep manual including ACB, AGV, CB, FCC, FPM, HMI, LED, LOTO, and PCA.

name: OptiSweep Manual Scope
description: The OptiSweep Operation and Maintenance Manual pertains exclusively to the FORTNA Inc. OptiSweep system.

name: OptiSweep Manual Chapter Structure
description: The OptiSweep manual is comprised of six chapters plus appendices covering safety, overview, operation, troubleshooting, maintenance, and service requests.

name: OptiSweep System Overview
description: The OptiSweep Sorter Sweeper system is a tote-to-person, smalls sorting system that works in conjunction with a customer's existing sorter. It consists of three main mechanical components (Geek+ P40 V2.0 robots, tippers, and a hospital station), a WCS controller, and an operator interface.

name: OptiSweep AGV Specification
description: The OptiSweep system uses Geek+ P40 (V2.0) AGVs. Detailed specifications are in the P40A (V2.0) user manual, Document version: V1.1 (20231206).

name: OptiSweep Hospital Station Function
description: The hospital station is a component of the OptiSweep system used to handle exceptions such as mis-sorts, bad tips, or tote overloads. AGVs deliver problem totes to the right side for operator handling and pick up empty totes from the left side.

name: OptiSweep Tipper Operation
description: Tippers are mechanical components that receive totes from AGVs and deposit parcels into bags via a chute. The tipper's gripper senses the tote and pulls it onto the tipper.

name: OptiSweep WCS and Sorter PLC Interaction
description: The WCS controller communicates with the customer's existing sorter PLC to control parcel diversion into totes based on weight, parcel count, or volume thresholds.

name: OptiSweep AGV Reference
description: The OptiSweep system uses Geek+ P40 (V2.0) AGVs. Detailed specifications are available in the P40A (V2.0) user manual, Document version: V1.1 (20231206).

name: OptiSweep WCS Controller
description: The WCS (Warehouse Control System) controller is a core component of the OptiSweep system that coordinates the sorter PLC, AGVs, and tippers.

name: Operator Station Overview
description: The operator station is the area where an operator receives parcels from the tippers.

name: Operator Station Components
description: The operator station includes seven key components: tipper, chute, stacklight, plastic curtain, operator station HMI, push-buttons, and rotary station.

name: Operator Station HMI
description: An HMI screen is located at the operator station.

name: Operator Station Stacklights
description: Two stacklights are mounted on the top of the operator station frame on either side of the chute.

name: Tipper Push-Button Flashing and Cycle Behavior
description: Yellow and green push-buttons flash to indicate tote arrival and type, and only one tipper cycle can be initiated at a time.

name: Emergency Stop Button Usage
description: The emergency stop button is only used for imminent danger to personnel or equipment damage.

name: Operator Station Push-Button Descriptions
description: Table 3-2 describes the five push-buttons on the operator station: TIP LEFT, SURE POST LEFT, SURE POST RIGHT, TIP RIGHT, and Emergency Stop.

name: Tipper Overview
description: Tippers receive totes from AGVs, pull the tote up, and empty parcels into a chute. Right and left tippers are identical but assembled as mirror images, with orientation based on the operator's perspective.

name: Tipper Components
description: The tipper assembly consists of 14 identified components including upper and lower hard stops, Z-axis and A-axis motors and cable carriers, a CLINK controller cover, column, sub-plate, counterbalances, counterbalance carriage, timing belt, air valve connection junction box, and gripper.

name: Tipper Gripper Operation
description: The tipper gripper senses the tote and pulls it up the tipper to empty parcels into a chute.

name: Hospital Station Overview
description: The Hospital Station is a manual handling station for totes that have experienced a mis-sort, bad tip, or tote overload. The WCS directs the AGV to bring the problematic tote to this station for operator intervention.

name: Hospital Station Operator Workflow
description: The operator workflow at the Hospital Station involves the AGV delivering a tote to the right side, the operator scanning the tote to determine the reason for arrival, and then placing an empty tote on the AGV on the left side before it returns to the sorter area.

name: Hospital Station Green Scanner
description: A green scanner is used by the operator at the Hospital Station to determine the reason a tote was brought to the station.

name: Hospital Station Stacklight
description: A stacklight at the Hospital Station indicates when a tote is present.

name: AGV Present Indicator at Hospital Station
description: A flashing yellow stacklight for 15 seconds indicates that an AGV is present at either position of the hospital station.

name: RMS Error Indicator at Hospital Station
description: The hospital station stacklight illuminates red, yellow, and green simultaneously to indicate an RMS error.

name: Fault Indicator at Hospital Station
description: A flashing red stacklight at the hospital station indicates a fault condition.

name: OptiSweep HMI Interfaces
description: The OptiSweep system is controlled through three Human-Machine Interface (HMI) panels: the System HMI, the Operator Station HMI, and the Hospital HMI.

name: System HMI Overview Screens
description: The System HMI includes four overview screens that display color-coded statuses for different areas of the system.

name: ACB System Overview Screen
description: The ACB System overview screen shows the tilt-tray system layout and a color-coded status of each bin.

name: OptiSweep HMI Interfaces Overview
description: The OptiSweep system is controlled through three distinct Human-Machine Interface (HMI) panels: the System HMI, the Operator Station HMI, and the Hospital HMI.

name: ACB System Overview Screen Navigation
description: The ACB System overview screen is accessed from the System HMI by navigating through SMALLS > ACB > ACB1 - AMT TT.

name: Building Overview Screen
description: The Building Overview screen displays the layout of the entire facility with a color-coded status for each area.

name: ACB System Overview Screen Legend
description: The legend for the ACB System Overview screen defines the color-coded statuses for system components.

name: Smalls Overview Screen
description: The Smalls overview screen is an HMI screen that displays the smalls system layout and provides a color-coded status for each part of the system.

name: ACB System Statistics Screen
description: The ACB System Statistics screen provides statistical information for the Automated Carton Buffer subsystem, including robot faults, system faults, cycle time, and tipping station bag counts.

name: ACB System Statistics Metrics
description: The ACB System Statistics screen displays metrics for robot faults, system faults, cycle time, and tipping station bag counts.

name: ACB System Screen Navigation
description: The ACB System Statistics screen is accessed by pressing the STATISTICS button on the ACB System screen.

name: HMI Calculations Screen
description: The HMI Calculations screen provides a Tilt Tray overview with information on system operations, bin statistics, and tipper statistics.

name: HMI Calculations Screen Navigation
description: The HMI Calculations screen is accessed by pressing the HMI CALCULATIONS button on the ACB System screen.

name: Tilt Tray Overview Screen
description: The HMI Calculations screen is also referred to as the Tilt Tray overview screen.

name: Tipping Station Screen Overview
description: The Tipping Station screen provides operational information on bag completion counts, errors, and task durations for the tipping station.

name: Tipping Station Screen Navigation Path
description: The navigation path to access the Tipping Station screen is: SMALLS > ACB > ACB1 - AMT TT > tipper button.

name: Tipping Station Screen Metrics
description: The Tipping Station screen displays metrics for bags completed, errors, and task duration.

name: ACB API Screen
description: The ACB API Screen is an HMI screen that provides controls for the OptiSweep system, AGVs, and totes.

name: OptiSweep System Control
description: The OptiSweep system can be controlled through the ACB API Screen.

name: AGV Control
description: AGVs can be controlled through the ACB API Screen.

name: Tote Control
description: Totes can be controlled through the ACB API Screen.

name: System API Controls Screen
description: The System API Controls screen is part of the System section of the API screen. It provides controls to manage the operational state of the OptiSweep system, including starting up, shutting down, closing out, and purging. It also displays the current system state and provides access to metrics and zone configuration.

name: System Shutdown Control
description: The System Shutdown control on the System API Controls screen shuts down the OptiSweep system. When activated, AGVs are sent to a shutdown queue. This action should only be performed when a sort does not begin when the current sort ends.

name: System Close Out Control
description: The System Close Out control on the System API Controls screen sends all totes to the tippers to close out the sorter. This action should only be performed at the end of a sort.

name: System Purge Control
description: The System Purge control on the System API Controls screen sends all totes to the tippers. Labels are not printed during a purge.

name: Get Metrics Pop-Up Screen
description: The Get Metrics pop-up screen is accessed by clicking the GET METRICS button on the System API Controls screen. It displays several operational metrics, including Number of Exchanges, Number of Mis-sorts, and Status.

name: Zone Configuration Pop-Up Screen
description: The Zone Configuration pop-up screen is accessed by clicking the ZONE CONFIGURATION button on the System API Controls screen. It lists the lane and zone for each AGV.

name: AGV API Controls Screen
description: The AGV API Controls screen, part of the System HMI, provides operators with controls to manage AGVs, including removing, recovering, pausing, and resuming AGVs, as well as executing commands and resending commands to Geek+.

name: AGV Remove and Recover Procedure
description: To remove an AGV from the system, an operator enters the AGV ID on the AGV API Controls screen. The AGV must be physically removed, and any carried tote must be taken to the hospital for removal and later recovery.

name: Get AGV Status Pop-Up Screen
description: The Get AGV Status pop-up screen, accessed from the AGV API Controls screen, displays detailed information for each AGV, including battery status, command status, error codes, and current state.

name: AGV System Recovery Commands
description: The AGV API Controls screen provides two commands for system recovery: 'Execute AGV Command' for when the system goes down and messages are missed, and 'Resend Geek Command' for resending a command to Geek+ after a command error.

name: Tote API Controls Screen
description: The Tote API Controls screen is a System HMI screen that provides manual controls for tote movement within the OptiSweep system.

name: Tote Exchange Settings Pop-Up Screen
description: The Tote Exchange Settings pop-up screen, accessed from the Tote API Controls, allows users to view and configure parameters for the automated tote exchange process.

name: Tote Exchange Modes
description: The OptiSweep system supports three distinct modes for automated tote exchange: Count, Cube, and Cube & Count.

name: Tote Exchange Thresholds
description: The Tote Exchange Settings screen defines multiple configurable thresholds that govern AGV pickup, exchange prioritization, and chute closure based on cube, item count, and weight.

name: AGV Status Screen
description: The AGV Status screen is an HMI screen that displays the real-time location of all AGVs and any active error codes they are experiencing.

name: AGV Status Screen Navigation
description: The AGV Status screen is accessed by pressing the AGV STATUS button in the upper-left corner of the main display.

name: AGV Error Code Display
description: The AGV Status screen displays any error codes that an AGV is currently experiencing.

name: Operator Station HMI Screen Location
description: An HMI screen is located on the right side of each tipper station.

name: Operator Station HMI Navigation Methods
description: HMI screens can be navigated using a drop-down menu, on-screen buttons, or physical display buttons.

name: Operator Station Primary Screens
description: Station operators primarily use the main control panel screen (F3), the data screen (F5), and the alarms screen (F6).

name: Operator Station Function Key Screen Mapping
description: Physical function keys F1-F6 map to specific HMI screens.

name: Operator Station Selection and Navigation Controls
description: Arrow buttons and a center select button are used for on-screen item navigation and selection.

name: Tipper Machine Control Panel (Visu_MCP_Dual) Screen Overview
description: The Visu_MCP_Dual screen is the primary operator station HMI for controlling the tipper. It provides buttons for automatic and manual control, fault reset, and axis referencing, with active buttons indicated by illuminated green bars.

name: Visu_MCP_Dual AUTO Button
description: The AUTO button on the Visu_MCP_Dual screen runs the tipper in automatic mode.

name: Visu_MCP_Dual JOG Button
description: The JOG button on the Visu_MCP_Dual screen allows manual control of the end effector and gripper position. Only maintenance personnel should use this function.

name: Visu_MCP_Dual Axis Position Indicators (A1, Z1, A2, Z2)
description: The Visu_MCP_Dual screen displays current axis positions in steps for the left gripper (A1, Z1) and right gripper (A2, Z2). A green 'R' circle indicates the axis has been referenced; a yellow data field indicates axis motion.

name: Visu_MCP_Dual Feedrate Override
description: The Feedrate Override on the Visu_MCP_Dual screen displays the tipper speed. In Auto mode, it should be set to 100%. Maintenance personnel may adjust it for troubleshooting.

name: Visu_MCP_Dual Fault and E-Stop Reset Sequence
description: After a fault, press RESET then CYCLE START to restart the tipper cycle. After an E-stop, press ESTOP RESET, then AUTO, then CYCLE START to restart the system.

name: VISU_DATA Screen Overview
description: The VISU_DATA screen is the main data screen on the Operator Station HMI. It provides a comprehensive view of tipper statistics, process status, runtime meters, operator performance, and heartbeat communication signals.

name: Tipper Stats Metrics
description: The Tipper Stats section on the VISU_DATA screen displays throughput and fault metrics for the left and right tippers, including totes processed, totes sent to the hospital, fault counts, average cycle time, average totes per hour, and time starved.

name: Process Status Indicators
description: The Process Status section on the VISU_DATA screen provides boolean status indicators for the tipper's operational state, including In Cycle, Tipper Ready, AGV Present, Tip in Process, Tipper Clear, and Tipper Faulted.

name: Operator Stats Response Time Metrics
description: The Operator Stats section on the VISU_DATA screen displays operator response time metrics in milliseconds for initiating tipping after a tote is gripped, including maximum, minimum, and average times for both left and right tippers.

name: Heartbeat Stats Metrics
description: The Heartbeat Stats section on the VISU_DATA screen displays communication signal timing metrics between the tipper and WCS, including Last, Max, and Min times in milliseconds. A heartbeat signal longer than 10 seconds can cause tipper operation issues.

name: VISU_DATA Screen Manual Controls
description: The VISU_DATA screen includes manual operator controls for sending totes to the hospital and pausing tippers, as well as user login/logout functions.

name: VISU_MANCONTROL Screen Overview
description: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen is an Operator Station HMI screen that provides manual controls for the OptiSweep system. The view shown is what personnel logged in as maintenance will see.

name: VISU_MANCONTROL Informational Banner
description: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen contains an informational banner (Item 1) that displays alarms or informational messages. Arrows on the right side of the banner allow navigation through messages.

name: LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET Button
description: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen has LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER FAULT RESET buttons (Item 6) that reset the corresponding tipper after a fault.

name: LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE Button
description: The VISU_MANCONTROL screen has LEFT/RIGHT TIPPER DISABLE buttons (Item 7) that disable the corresponding tipper. Activating this button causes the stacklight to illuminate solid blue.

name: CellIO Status Screen
description: The CELLIO STATUS button (Item 9) on the VISU_MANCONTROL screen opens a sub-screen containing the cell control input and output values per tipper.

name: wCommand Screen
description: The WCOMMAND button (Item 10) on the VISU_MANCONTROL screen opens a sub-screen displaying the input and output Command Word values for the respective tipper to the WCS. A NEXT SIDE button allows navigation between the left and right tipper views.

name: VISU_MDS (Machine Data) Screen Overview
description: The VISU_MDS screen on the Operator Station HMI displays all parameters for each axis (Z1, A1, Z2, A2) of the OptiSweep machine. Parameters generally do not require changing unless a motor is replaced.

name: OptiSweep Machine Axes (Z1, A1, Z2, A2)
VISU_MDS Axis Parameter Definitions
description: The VISU_MDS screen defines specific Machine Data (MD) IDs for axis parameters including positions, limits, speeds, and accelerations used in auto-cycle and jog operations.
aliases: MD6 Plus Travel Opposite Axis Position
MD7 Neg Travel Opposite Axis Position

name: VISU_MDS COPY FROM OPPOSITE Function
description: The COPY FROM OPPOSITE button on the VISU_MDS screen copies axis parameters from one tipper to the selected axis on the opposite tipper.

name: VISU_MDS Unique Axis Parameters
description: MD5 (Tote Pickup Position) and MD21 (Home Offset) are unique for every machine and every axis, measured during operator station alignment procedures.

name: VISU_IO_DIAG Screen Overview
description: The VISU_IO_DIAG screen on the Operator Station HMI is a read-only screen used for troubleshooting. It provides diagnostic information about the HMI hardware and connected I/O.

name: VISU_IO_DIAG Control Temps Section
description: The 'Control Temps' section on the VISU_IO_DIAG screen displays the temperature readings of the CPU and the motherboard (MB) inside the HMI.

name: VISU_IO_DIAG Voltage Levels Section
description: The 'Voltage Levels' section on the VISU_IO_DIAG screen displays the voltage readings of the HMI's internal controller, which should be 24 V.

name: VISU_IO_DIAG Switch Status Section
description: A section on the VISU_IO_DIAG screen corresponds to the switch mounted on the station and conveys which inputs are on and off.

name: VISU_IO_DIAG Input Details Pop-up
description: Selecting an input section on the VISU_IO_DIAG screen opens a window providing more information on what the inputs are.

name: VISU_ALARM Screen
description: The Visu_Alarm screen on the Operator Station HMI displays a list of all tipper alarms with timestamps.

name: VISU_ALARM History Capacity
description: The Visu_Alarm screen's SHOW HISTORY function can display up to the last 1500 alarm records.

name: Tipper Alarms on Operator Station HMI
description: Tipper alarms are displayed on the Operator Station HMI Visu_Alarm screen with timestamps.

name: Hospital HMI Purpose
description: The Hospital HMI screens are used to handle totes that have been directed to the Hospital Station.

name: Hospital HMI Main Menu Controls
description: The Hospital HMI Main Menu has six function button controls for navigation.

name: Hospital HMI Operations Screen
description: The Hospital HMI Operations Screen displays read-only information from the WCS for the induct and extract positions at a hospital station. It shows AGV ID, Tote ID, Bar Code, and Status messages for each position.

name: Hospital HMI Induct Position Fields
description: The Induct Position section of the Hospital HMI Operations Screen displays four read-only fields from the WCS: AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and Status.

name: Hospital HMI Extract Position Fields
description: The Extract Position section of the Hospital HMI Operations Screen displays four read-only fields from the WCS: AGV#, Tote ID, Bar Code, and Status.

name: Hospital HMI WCS Status Messages
description: The Status field on the Hospital HMI Operations Screen displays messages from the WCS that tell the station operator why a tote is at the station and what action to perform.

name: Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu Screen
description: The Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu screen provides access to four maintenance functions: Manual Control, IO Diagnostics, Persistent Variables, and Default.

name: Hospital HMI Manual Control Access
description: The Manual Control function (2.1) is accessible from the Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu.

name: Hospital HMI IO Diagnostics Access
description: The IO Diagnostics function (2.2) is accessible from the Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu.

name: Hospital HMI Persistent Variables Access
description: The Persistent Variables function (2.3) is accessible from the Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu.

name: Hospital HMI Default Access
description: The Default function (2.4) is accessible from the Hospital HMI Maintenance Menu.

name: Hospital HMI 2.2 IO Diagnostics Screen
description: The Hospital HMI 2.2 IO Diagnostics screen displays the state of inputs from the switch mounted on the station and provides temperature and voltage readings for the HMI itself.

name: Hospital HMI 2.4 Default Screen
description: The Hospital HMI 2.4 Default screen displays the currently installed software version and the IP address of the Hospital Station, and provides user login/logout functionality.

name: Hospital HMI REBOOT TO SETUP Function
description: The REBOOT TO SETUP button on the Hospital HMI Default screen is restricted to maintenance personnel for updating the HMI's date or time.

name: Hospital HMI Alarms Screen
description: The Alarms screen on the Hospital HMI provides a list of all system alarms along with a time stamp.

name: Alarm Table Structure
description: Alarms are defined using a table with columns for Text List, ID, Alarm Text, Cause, Controller Response, and Corrective Action.

name: Left Tipper Alarm Group
description: The Left Tipper has a dedicated alarm group (AlarmGroup_Helix_LeftTipper) with specific alarms for E-Stop, cycle states, faults, and operator requests.

name: Right Tipper Alarm Group
description: The Right Tipper has a dedicated alarm group (AlarmGroup_Helix_RightTipper) mirroring the Left Tipper's alarms for E-Stop, cycle states, and faults.

name: Hospital Request Alarm
description: A 'Hospital Request' alarm (ID 18 for Left Tipper) is generated when a manual or automatic request is made to send a tote to the hospital for diagnosis.

name: Tipper Cycle Stop Alarm
description: A 'Tipper Cycle Stopped' alarm (ID 13) indicates the operator station is in a Cycle Stopped state, requiring a CYCLE START or RESET command.

name: OptiSweep System Operation Overview
description: The OptiSweep Sorter Sweeper is primarily operated by the WCS (Warehouse Control System). Manual intervention is limited to the tipper and hospital stations.

name: System Startup via HMI
description: To start the OptiSweep system, an operator must navigate to the system API screen on the HMI and press the SYSTEM STARTUP button.

name: HMI System API Screen
description: The system HMI contains a 'system API screen' which is used to initiate a system startup.

name: Operator Station Startup Prerequisites
description: Before starting the operator station, verify AGVs are powered on and the main disconnect is ON.

name: Operator Station E-Stop Reset
description: If the ESTOP is flashing at the operator station control panel, pull out the ESTOP and press RESET on the HMI screen to clear faults.

name: Tipper Axis Homing (Z1/A1, Z2/A2)
description: The operator station has two tippers (left and right), each with Z and A axes that must be homed using AUTO REF.

name: Tipper Cycle Start to Ready Position
description: After homing, pressing CYCLE START moves the tipper motor from the home position to the ready position.

name: Tipper AUTO Mode
description: Placing the tipper in AUTO mode allows it to wait for and receive instructions from the WCS.

name: Operator Station Shutdown (CYCLE STOP)
description: To stop the operator station, press CYCLE STOP on the operator station main screen.

name: Operator Station Stop Procedure
description: The procedure to stop the operator station is to press the CYCLE STOP button on the operator station main screen.

name: Operator Station Startup Procedure
description: The operator station startup procedure involves verifying AGV power, checking the main disconnect, clearing E-STOP faults, homing axes, and placing the tipper in AUTO mode.

name: System Shutdown Procedure
description: The system shutdown procedure is initiated from the system HMI API screen by pressing SYSTEM SHUTDOWN, which sends AGVs to a shutdown queue.

name: Operator Station HMI CYCLE STOP Button
description: The operator station main screen contains a CYCLE STOP button used to stop the operator station.

name: Tipper Jogging Mode
description: The tipper end effector can be manually moved for maintenance using the HMI's jogging mode.

name: Tipper Jogging HMI Screen
description: The jogging screen is part of the 'Visu_Dual_MCP' interface and provides manual controls for the tipper axes.

name: Tipper Axis Hard Stop Fault
description: A fault is registered if a tipper axis is pushed to its hard stop during jogging.

name: Non-Recoverable Faults Overview
description: Non-recoverable faults are faults that cannot be recovered via software and require a manual reset at the operator station.

name: Operator Station Motor Fault Recovery
description: Recovery from a non-recoverable motor fault on an operator station tipper involves stopping the cycle via the HMI.

name: HMI MCP_Dual Screen (F3)
description: The 'MCP_Dual' screen, accessed via F3 on the operator station HMI, contains the CYCLE STOP control used during fault recovery.

name: HMI CYCLE STOP Control
description: The CYCLE STOP button on the operator station HMI is used to stop the tipping cycle during a fault recovery process.

name: Non-Recoverable Fault: Operator Station Motors
description: A non-recoverable fault, such as a motor overload on a tipper, requires a manual reset at the operator station HMI. The recovery process involves stopping the cycle, entering manual jog mode, clearing axis faults, repositioning the tote, and then returning to automatic mode to release the tote and send the robot to the hospital station.

name: MCP_Dual Screen (F3)
description: The MCP_Dual screen (F3) on the operator station HMI is the primary interface for manual control and fault recovery for the operator station motors. It provides controls for CYCLE STOP, JOG, RESET, AUTO, CYCLE START, and axis jogging (Z1, Z2, A1, A2).

name: Operator Station Axes (Z1, Z2, A1, A2)
description: The operator station tipper has four axes: Z1, Z2, A1, and A2. A1 and Z1 control the left tipper, while A2 and Z2 control the right tipper. These axes can be manually jogged during fault recovery to reposition a tote.

name: Non-Recoverable Fault: AGV Stuck
description: A non-recoverable fault indicating an AGV remains at the tipper after tote-tipping is complete, likely due to a communication issue.

name: HMI Screen: Visu_ManControl
description: An operator station HMI screen used to access the CellIO Status for troubleshooting faults like an AGV stuck at a tipper.

name: HMI Screen: CellIO Status
description: An operator station HMI screen accessed from Visu_ManControl that displays I/O status for a selected tipper, including OUT Fault Status and forced value controls for OUT W1.

name: AGV Stuck Fault Status Value: 82
description: The OUT Fault Status value of 82 on the CellIO Status screen indicates a non-recoverable AGV stuck fault at a tipper.

name: OUT W1 Forced Values for AGV Stuck Recovery
description: Forcing a value on OUT W1 on the CellIO Status screen is used to recover from an AGV stuck fault. A value of 3 allows the AGV to continue, while 32771 sends it to the hospital.

name: AGV System Start-Up Prerequisites
description: Before starting the OptiSweep system, ensure nine AGVs without totes are positioned: five under the north rack and four under the south rack. If fewer than nine are present, an AGV without a tote must be moved into the deficient zone and added to the RMS.

name: System Start-Up Timing Requirement
description: The OptiSweep system must be started 15 minutes before the sort begins.

name: System Start-Up Sequence
description: The system start-up sequence consists of resetting metrics, starting the system, performing close out (Bag Out), after which the system returns to 'Running' state, and then shutting down.

name: System 'Running' State After Close Out
description: After the close out (Bag Out) procedure is completed, the OptiSweep system transitions back to the 'Running' state.

name: AGV System Start-Up Precondition
description: Before starting the OptiSweep system, a specific number of AGVs without totes must be present in designated zones.

name: AGV System Start-Up Sequence
description: The high-level sequence for starting the AGV system involves resetting metrics, starting the system, and performing a close out (Bag Out).

name: System Status: Running
description: The 'Running' status is the normal operating state the system returns to after the close out (Bag Out) process is completed during start-up.

name: HMI Screen: System in Shut-down Mode
description: A system screen exists showing the 'System in Shut-down Mode' state, referenced in the AGV start-up procedure.

name: Required Information Before Entering the Dance Floor
description: Before entering the grid (Dance Floor) for fault recovery, personnel must have the Robot ID, fault description from RMS, tote ID if the AGV is holding a bin, and confirmation if a faulted AGV under a rack is the empty AGV for that zone.

name: AGV Bump Fault Exception Codes
description: Two exception codes are defined for AGV 'Bump' faults: 21057 (Robot front collision bar triggers) and 21060 (The robot triggers the obstacle avoidance).

name: AGV RESET Button
description: The AGV has a RESET button that can be clicked for two seconds to clear a fault.

name: RMS E-Stop
description: The RMS has an E-stop function that can be activated and deactivated.

name: AGV Bump Fault Screen
description: The AGV Bump Fault Screen is an RMS interface that displays exception information for bump-related faults, including codes 21057 and 21060.

name: Fault Recovery Prerequisite Information
description: Before entering the grid (Dance Floor) for fault recovery, the operator must gather the Robot ID, fault description from RMS, whether the AGV is holding a bin (and its Tote ID), and if a faulted AGV under a rack is the empty AGV for that zone.

name: AGV 'szonestaging' State
description: The 'szonestaging' state is a required AGV status for certain recovery procedures. It is verified on the HMI and indicates the AGV is correctly staged in its zone.

name: AGVS Lost Tasks Recovery Procedure Reference
description: A fault recovery procedure exists for when empty AGVs lose their tasks after an RMS restart. The procedure involves E-stopping RMS, removing and re-adding AGVs twice, ensuring they are in 'szonestaging' state, and resuming RMS.

name: Tote API Controls Reference
description: The 'Tote API Controls' is a function within RMS used to add or remove AGVs during fault recovery procedures.

name: AGV 'Hospital' Destination State
description: The 'Hospital' is an undesired AGV destination state during the 'Add AGV to Zone' recovery procedure. If an AGV is moving to the Hospital, it must be removed and re-added.

name: AGV 'Blue' Status Indicator
description: An AGV turning 'blue' is a visual indicator on the HMI that confirms a successful state change after being manually added to a zone during fault recovery.

name: Faulted AGV with Tote Recovery Concept
description: A recovery concept exists for a faulted AGV carrying a tote on the RMS: stop the RMS, remove the AGV, take the tote to the Hospital for manual removal, re-add the AGV, and resume the RMS.

name: AGV Fault During Exchange Recovery Concept
description: A recovery concept exists for when an AGV faults during an exchange on the RMS: stop the RMS, remove the faulted AGV, and potentially introduce a new tote and empty AGV at the location.
aliases: AGV Fault During Exchange Recovery Concept

name: AGV Lost Tote (No Fault) Recovery Concept
description: A recovery concept exists for an AGV that has lost a tote but has not faulted: stop the RMS, manually move the AGV to the Hospital for a system reset, and re-introduce the lost tote.

name: Hospital Station PC
description: The Hospital station includes a PC used for managing AGVs, specifically for removing and adding them back into the system during recovery procedures.

name: AGV Brake Release
description: AGVs have a physical brake release that can be pressed to allow the AGV to be manually pushed, such as when moving it to the Hospital station.

name: Inbound Hospital Station QR Code
description: A QR code located in front of the Inbound Hospital Station used to re-initialize an AGV's position after a recovery procedure.

name: AGV Green Lights Status
description: Green lights on an AGV indicate a ready or operational status after a power cycle, signaling that the AGV can be positioned over a QR code for localization.

name: Hospital Station HMI Screen
description: An HMI screen is used to extract a tote from the system at the Hospital Station. The screen is opened based on information in status fields.

name: Hospital Station Manual Task Performance
description: After a tote is extracted at the Hospital Station, an operator performs a task as determined by information in the status fields.

name: Sorter Scanner Overview
description: The Zebra scanner is a hand-held device used at the sorter for manual tote management operations.

name: Sorter Tote Replacement Rule
description: When a tote is manually removed from the sorter stand, it must be returned to its original position with the same Tote ID.

name: Sorter Scanner Use Cases
description: The Zebra scanner at the sorter is used for tote replacement, maintenance, repair, and handling damaged totes.

name: E-Stop Zone Reset Procedure
description: The standard procedure for clearing an obstruction or faulted AGV involves referencing the E-stop zone map, pressing the appropriate E-STOP to stop the zone, removing the obstruction or AGV, pulling the E-STOP, and pressing the blue RESET button to resume system operation.

name: Operator Station Daily Preventive Maintenance
description: Daily preventive maintenance checks for the operator station include inspecting the controller for damage, verifying stacklights are operational, and ensuring the chute is free of debris such as stuck labels.

name: Hospital Station Daily Preventive Maintenance
description: Daily preventive maintenance checks for each hospital station include verifying the barcode scanner is operational, the stacklight is operational, and the tabletop is free of debris.

name: Maintenance References for P40 Robots and Tipper
description: For maintenance related to P40 (V2.0) robots, reference the P40A (V2.0) user manual. For tipper maintenance, contact Lifecycle Performance Services (LPS) at 888-444-4647.

name: Daily Preventive Maintenance for Operator Station
description: Daily inspection checklist for the OptiSweep operator station.

name: Daily Preventive Maintenance for Hospital Station
description: Daily inspection checklist for each OptiSweep hospital station.

name: Maintenance Support Contacts
description: Contact references for maintenance of P40 robots and the tipper.

name: Operator Station Daily Preventive Maintenance Inspection
description: Daily preventive maintenance for the operator station includes inspecting the controller for damage, verifying stacklights are operational, and ensuring the chute is free of debris such as stuck labels.

name: Operator Station Chute Debris
description: A known issue for the operator station chute is the accumulation of debris, specifically stuck labels.

name: Hospital Station Daily Inspection Items
description: Daily preventive maintenance inspection items for each hospital station.

name: Tipper Preventive Maintenance Schedule
description: Defines the escalating schedule for tipper inspections after the system goes live: weekly for the first four weeks, then monthly for four months, then every 6 months thereafter.

name: Tipper Z-Axis Linear Bearings Inspection and Lubrication
description: Procedure for visually inspecting Z-axis linear rails for grease wetness and lubricating bearing blocks if rails are dry, using automotive bearing grease.

name: Tipper Inspection Checklist Reference
description: A Tipper Inspection Checklist exists on page 209 of the manual and should be used during tipper inspections to avoid missing important tasks.

name: Daily Maintenance Checklist
description: A daily inspection and maintenance checklist for the OptiSweep system, covering the Operator Station controller, chute, stacklights, guards, and QR codes.

name: Tipper Preventive Maintenance Inspection Schedule
description: The schedule for tipper preventive maintenance inspections after the system is live: weekly for the first four weeks, monthly for four months, then every 6 months.

name: Z-Axis Linear Bearing Lubrication
description: Procedure for visually inspecting and lubricating the Z-axis linear bearings on the tipper, including grease type and quantity.

name: Tipper Re-commissioning Requirement After Part Replacement
description: A tipper must be re-commissioned after any part is replaced.

name: Automatic Axes Referencing Procedure
description: Procedure to automatically reference all axes of the tippers using the HMI.

name: Manual Axes Referencing Initiation
description: The end effector can be manually moved into position for maintenance using the HMI.

name: Stacklight Replacement Overview
description: The stacklight is a replaceable three-segment component on the OptiSweep system. Replacement requires a 7-mm wrench, safety glasses, gloves, and approximately 30 minutes.

name: Stacklight M12 Connector
description: The stacklight uses an M12 connector for its electrical connection.

name: Tipper Replacement Overview
description: The tipper is a replaceable component on the OptiSweep operator station. Replacement involves LOTO, disconnecting power, Ethernet, and air lines, removing the old tipper from the sub-plate, and installing a new one.

name: Tipper Connections
description: The tipper has three external connections: a 6-pin Molex power connector, an Ethernet cable to the ClearLink controller, and an air line with a quick disconnect at the bottom of the column.

name: Tipper Mounting
description: The tipper is secured to a sub-plate using four hex head screws. A side panel provides access to the motor.

name: Tipper Replacement Prerequisites
description: Tipper replacement requires LOTO of the tipper, PPE (safety glasses, gloves), and a replacement tipper part. Optional removal of the gripper and counter-balance weights is recommended.

name: Tipper Commissioning Overview
description: When any tipper component is replaced, the tipper must be aligned with the other tipper to ensure grippers and axes are level. The commissioning process involves 12 high-level steps, from applying power to validating setup.

name: Tipper Commissioning Tools and Personnel Requirements
description: Tipper commissioning requires two people, three hours, and specific tools: a level, digital measure, large square, and screwdriver.

name: HMI Screen: Visu_MDs (F2)
description: The 'Visu_MDs' screen, accessed via F2 on the operator station HMI, is used to set initial controller parameters for tipper axes during commissioning.

name: Tipper Tote Pickup Position
description: The tote pickup position for the tipper is set to 16 3/4 inches during commissioning.

name: Scanner Replacement Setup Procedure
description: When a scanner is replaced, the new scanner must be set up using a specific procedure involving a Windows laptop, a Zebra DS3608-SR scanner dock, and the Barcode Interface application.

name: Barcode Interface Application
description: The Barcode Interface application ('Barcode Interface.exe') is a desktop application used on a Windows laptop to set up and configure replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanners.

name: Scanner Setup Network Connectivity Requirements
description: Setting up a replacement scanner requires the setup laptop to have network connectivity to both the AGV control and Hospital control systems, validated by pinging their IP addresses.

name: Scanner Setup Hardware Requirements
description: The hardware required for setting up a replacement Zebra DS3608-SR scanner includes the scanner dock, a specific USB cable, a power adapter, and two 120 VAC outlets.

name: Barcode Interface Default Settings Password
description: The default password to access the settings in the Barcode Interface application is 'Opti'.
