OptiSweep training session identification
description: An introductory title slide identifies a UPS/FORTNA OptiSweep training session labeled Day 1.

name: OptiSweep training presenter reference
description: The title slide names Mitchel Flynn and Samuel Prescott as presenters or associated session personnel for the training.

name: Introductory title slide reference
description: The captured frame is a title or intro slide for the training video rather than an OptiSweep operational HMI screen.

name: Training session start and presenter introduction
description: This segment captures the informal start of a training session and the transition into the morning's slides, including a presenter introduction.

name: Pre-session room and attendance logistics
description: Informal discussion about attendee availability, audio check, Wi-Fi access, and room conditions occurs before the training begins.

name: Segment contains minimal OptiSweep operational content
description: This source segment is primarily conversational and does not provide stable technical details about OptiSweep systems, screens, alarms, or metrics.

name: OptiSweep overview introduction
description: This training segment introduces OptiSweep at a high level and frames the session as an overview for attendees who may not know the system.

name: Training scope is introductory rather than detailed
description: This segment indicates the training is being delivered at an introductory level for participants who may not already know the system.

name: Traditional small sort bagging operating model
description: A traditional small sort bagging system is operator-intensive, with operators assigned destination sections on a sorter and manually handling full bags.

name: Belted ACB solution bag flow description
description: In a belted ACB solution, a full destination bin is dropped onto a takeaway conveyor and conveyed as a slug to a chute and bag station.

name: OptiSweep modularity and existing sorter adaptation
description: The OptiSweep design goal is modularity and adaptation to existing building sorters with minimal modification.

name: OptiSweep software as the integration layer
description: OptiSweep software is the component that integrates multiple subsystems so they communicate and operate together.

name: Core elements shown in the OptiSweep overview architecture
description: The overview slide identifies the main components participating in the OptiSweep environment shown in this training segment.

name: Hospital controller role in tote removal and addition
description: The hospital controller is described as the component used to remove and add totes.

name: Geek+ AGV and RMS control architecture overview
description: Geek+ AGVs operate over QR codes and are directly controlled by Geek+ RMS, with RMS serving as the robot management layer that handles movement execution and route determination.

name: Obstacle reporting and alarm visibility in RMS
description: When an AGV detects an obstacle through its physical hardware, the condition is reported to RMS, which generates an alarm code visible on the RMS screen.

name: AGV safety-related operating characteristics
description: AGVs have forward collision sensors and are intended to operate in a fenced system.

name: Tote racking overview
description: Tote racks are the structure where the tote sits on the cylinder within the OptiSweep system.

name: Tote rack alignment features
description: The tote rack includes small feet that align a dropped tote to the center position.

name: Side fins for package centering
description: The tote rack includes side fins that help move packages toward the center if they strike off-center.

name: Tote rack design intent for parcel impact positioning
description: The training material describes the tote rack as a beveled design intended to securely position the tote for parcel impact.

name: Tipper station overview at operator stations
description: Each operator station has two tippers used to receive a tote from an AGV, clamp it, tip contents onto a chute, and return the tote.

name: Tipper mechanical handling functions
description: The tipper is described as a handling component that clamps a tote from an AGV, tips it to discharge contents onto a chute, and returns the tote to the AGV.

name: Self-contained HMI at the tipper station
description: The tipper station includes a self-contained HMI used for operation and fault recovery.

name: Emergency stop presence at tipper operation
description: An operator E-stop is part of the tipper station setup.

name: OptiSweep software environment overview
description: The main software elements around OptiSweep are: OptiSweep software as the integrating layer, AVEVA as the HMI, Ignition as the OPC server, Chat XLE for UPS communications, and S-Tunnel for secure connectivity between the OT network and the UPS network.

name: Ignition as the OPC server
description: Ignition is identified in the training material as the OPC server used in the OptiSweep software environment.

name: AVEVA as the HMI
description: AVEVA is identified as the HMI in the OptiSweep software stack and is described as directly integrating with the OPC server for data access.

name: Lifecycle of a sort overview
description: This training segment describes the high-level lifecycle of a sort in OptiSweep, moving from startup through bulk sorting, bag-out, and shutdown.

name: AGV startup and shutdown state behavior
description: AGVs are positioned and state-labeled at the beginning and end of a sort cycle.

name: Bulk sort and bag-out functions
description: The main sorting phase is distinct from the bag-out phase, each with its own role for AGVs and tippers.

name: State transition fault visibility during startup and shutdown
description: State transitions can fail and that the system exposes faults or visible waiting conditions during startup and shutdown.
aliases: AGV waiting to do an exchange

name: Parcel lifecycle into the sorter
description: The upstream parcel flow before and at sorter induction includes unloading from trailers, movement on belts, and arrival onto the sorter with associated data messages.

name: First Chat message parcel data
description: An initial message from Chat is triggered before sorter entry and carries core parcel attributes.

name: Unknown inducted parcels and default dimensions
description: When the first parcel message fails, an unknown inducted parcel is assigned default dimensions by OptiSweep.

name: Weight and dimensions support tote fullness assessment
description: Weight and dimensions are used by software when determining how full a tote or location is as items accumulate.

name: Upstream parcel data exchange into OptiSweep
Default dimensions for unknown inducted parcels
description: OptiSweep assigns default dimensions when the initial message fails and an unknown parcel is inducted.

name: Potential destination fields in parcel data
ZIP code to destination mapping is handled upstream
description: ZIP codes are mapped upstream to one or more destinations, and OptiSweep's local order context uses destination information rather than ZIP code logic.

name: Interpretation of destination data in local systems
Tote exchange operating concept
description: In an AGV tote exchange, one AGV moves out while another moves in so the exchange happens simultaneously.

name: Exchange staging thresholds for tote fullness
description: Exchange staging is associated with thresholds and can occur when a tote is imminently full or completely full.

name: Post-exchange AGV role transition
description: The AGV that drops its tote becomes the AGV that will pick up the next tote.

name: Chute opening timing and KPI emphasis
description: Chute opening timing is linked to exchange speed: the chute is opened when the AGV moves in rather than when it drops a tote, in support of strict KPI targets.

name: Tipper assignment and entrance queue concept
description: A full tote on an AGV is assigned to a tipper and routed through a tipper entrance queue using round-robin selection among available enabled tippers serviced by the queue.

name: Tip staging notification and controller interface
description: The handoff between AGV movement and the tipper controller includes AGV travel to the tip location and software notification over OPC that the AGV has staged for a tip.

name: AGV destinations after a completed cycle
description: After the full cycle is complete and the tipper indicates the AGV is clear to move, the AGV may return to the sorter, go to the hospital, or go to charge.

name: Sorter entrance queue return with empty tote
description: If no exception or charging condition applies, the AGV returns to the sorter entrance queue with an empty tote for the next exchange.

name: Hospital area for exception handling
description: The hospital is described as an area where AGBs are sent when the system cannot properly detect or grip a tote.

name: Hospital station staffing model
description: The hospital station is described as not being continuously manned, with supervisors or nearby tipper positions monitoring and handling hospital items.

name: Layout modularity and area-to-area movement model
description: The layout is described as modular and scalable, with distinct areas connected through entrance and exit points.

name: Named layout area types in the example design
description: The example layout identifies several area types, including Hospital, SorterSide, Charger, and Tipper.

name: Sorter queue layout and movement areas
description: The sorter layout includes distinct queue areas that structure how AGVs and totes move into, through, and out of the sorter area.

name: Shutdown queue locations and tote-dependent shutdown positioning
description: Shutdown uses designated queue locations, with different shutdown positions described for AGVs with totes and AGVs without totes, including an off-the-end path during shutdown entry.

name: Bag out as end-of-sort clearing activity
description: Bag out is described as the activity used at the end of a sort to remove remaining items from the system before the next sort configuration begins.

name: Sort phases require transitions between runs
description: The training describes sorter operation as occurring in distinct sort phases, with transitions between sorts because each sort has different volume and destination characteristics.

name: Sorter zones constrain AGV pickup and drop-off areas
description: The sorter side uses zones, and an AGV operates within its zone for pickup and drop-off activity.

name: Tipper queue and post-tip flow
description: Tipper A and tipper B are separate tip locations, each with its own tipper queue. After tipping, an AGV proceeds into the next part of the flow associated with the hospital area.

name: Hospital module flow and queue structure
description: The hospital area is described as having an entrance queue, drop-off behavior when the location is free, pickup behavior when a tote is available, and an exit queue after departure.

name: Shutdown-state AGV replacement behavior through hospital
description: A shutdown-state example is given in which removing an AGV without a tote and adding another AGV causes the added AGV to go through the hospital first and then determine where it is needed.

name: Charger module queue and tote handling
description: The charger area is described as having an entrance queue, tote drop-off locations, charging behavior without totes on the AGV, tote pickup after charging, and an exit queue.

name: Shutdown queues hold AGVs in shutdown state
description: Shutdown queues are described as the place where AGVs sit when the system is in shutdown, before startup returns them to their assigned zones.

name: Shutdown is selected from the HMI
description: Shutdown is not automatic at the end of bag out; it is a state chosen by the operator from the HMI.

name: Peak planning influences system behavior and sizing context
description: The training notes that some system behaviors and design choices are planned around peak operating conditions, including equipment counts and cycle timing considerations.

name: RMS home screen navigation overview
description: RMS home screen navigation elements include language selection, a collapsible sidebar menu, and access to the Map Monitor view.

name: RMS language selection control
description: The RMS interface includes a language selection control in the top-right corner that can be used to switch the interface to English when the default language appears in Chinese.

name: RMS sidebar menu expansion and collapse
description: The RMS interface includes a sidebar menu that may be hidden and can be expanded or collapsed for navigation.

name: Map Monitor screen purpose
description: Map Monitor is presented as a primary RMS screen and is described as the place where users are likely to spend most of their time.

name: Map overview provides a system-level view
description: A clickable map overview gives an overview of the system and is used to visually separate major areas such as sorter, charger, and tipper sides.

name: Map Monitor message panel overview
description: A Map Monitor message panel on the right side of the interface lists several robot and AGV status and fault-related items.

name: Robot count metrics shown in the message panel
description: The message panel includes count-based metrics for active robots and robots charging.

name: Open message panel and alarm history view
description: The map monitor summary area includes an open message panel used to view pending messages containing active errors or warnings, along with recent alarm history.

name: Robot count summary metrics on the map monitor
description: The summary area presents counts for actively running robots and robots currently charging.

name: Drop-down area for current AGV faults
description: A small drop-down in the summary area can reveal current faults that need attention when they are present.

name: Disconnected AGV count and RMS communication concept
description: The disconnected AGV count shows how many AGVs the RMS considers disconnected due to lost communication or other causes such as being turned off.

name: Terminology distinction between turned off and shutdown
description: The training distinguishes an AGV being turned off from the term shutdown, which is described as a specific OptiSweep operational state term.

name: Map Monitor Quick Select icons overview
description: The Map Monitor Quick Select area contains icons used to visualize AGV paths, display station and charger IDs, and choose which map object type is selectable for inspection.

name: AGV active path visualization on the map
description: The View all AGV active paths icon displays active AGV routes on the map as blue lines from each AGV to its destination.

name: Station IDs as unique map location identifiers
description: Stations are treated as special map locations with unique IDs, distinct from cells, and AGVs can be directed between stations using those IDs.

name: Charger IDs as unique charger identifiers
description: Chargers in the system have unique IDs, and the map can display those charger IDs.

name: Map object selection modes for clickable items
description: Because multiple object types exist on the map, users must choose a selection mode before clicking map items to inspect them.

name: Robot selection panel overview
description: The Robot selection view allows an operator to click a robot and see robot-specific details in an expandable detail panel.

name: Robot detail fields shown after selection
description: The robot detail area includes identifiers and location-related fields such as robot ID, location, node code, and tote ID when present.

name: Tote presence indicators on robot selection
description: The robot selection display uses tote text and visual cues to indicate whether a robot is carrying a tote, has a tote mismatch after robot removal, or has no tote.

name: Robot LED color status meanings
description: Robot LED colors indicate connection, task, label-search, idle, and fault or low-battery states.

name: Robot Selection Add and Remove screen
description: A training slide titled "Robot Selection Add and Remove" presents interface options for adding or removing a robot by robot ID or selection.

name: Success indication for robot add and remove actions
description: The system provides a success indication after robot add and remove actions.

name: Robot Selection Restart Robot screen
description: A training slide shows a Robot Selection screen for restarting a robot. The screen content indicates that an operator can enter a robot ID or select a robot, then use a Restart action.

name: Robot restart position requirement
description: Robot restart is associated with a position requirement involving a restart point or a QR code cell.

name: Map display after robot restart
description: After starting, the positioned robot is displayed on the station map.

name: Geek Plus RMS access from the OT network
description: The training states that devices connected to the OT network can access the web application through its IP address.

name: Robot restart panel and selection inputs
description: A restart panel lets an operator enter a robot ID or select a robot, then use a Restart control to restart that robot.

name: Task persistence across restart versus removal
description: A robot's transaction resumes after restart unless the robot is removed from the system.

name: AGV Go-to function for manual repositioning
description: The Go-to function allows an AGV that is not currently in a task to be sent to another square or map cell, which is described as helpful for quick recovery and repositioning.

name: Hospital location as a recovery drop-off point
description: The hospital location is described as a preferred destination for sending an AGV during recovery because the tote can be dropped there and the AGV can then reinitialize and pick up a new tote.

name: Container and tote lookup by number or location
description: The Container Selection screen can be used to find a tote by entering a location number or tote number and identifying the rack or AGV where it is located.

name: Rack locations in the RMS/map view
description: Rack locations are selectable map elements in the RMS/container selection view, used to inspect rack-specific information.

name: Rack color indicates tote presence state
description: Two rack colors are used in the map view: dark blue/violet indicates a tote is present, and light blue indicates the rack is empty.

name: Floor QR code as a physical location marker
description: The floor QR code is described as having a physical number that corresponds to the node or cell code used for location verification.

name: Robot Selection Restart screen reference
description: A Robot Selection Restart screen is used to identify a robot by robot ID or selection and initiate a restart.

name: Restart position reference for robot restart
description: Robot restart is associated with the robot being at a restart point or on the QR code cell, and that the positioned robot is displayed after starting.

name: Container Selection screen overview
description: A Container Selection screen is used to view totes or containers, associated rack locations, and related identifiers within the system.

name: Container color indicators on the screen
description: Color coding indicates whether a rack location contains a tote.

name: Layer Count reflects single-density rack configuration
description: The Layer Count field is described in the training as reflecting the rack property configuration, and this site uses a single layer.

name: AGV object selection displays AGV-specific information
description: Selecting an AGV object in the interface causes AGV information to display.

name: Selected cell changes displayed rack information
description: The spoken training segment indicates that changing the display mode and selecting the same cell can show rack information.

name: Selected symbol conveys object meaning
description: Selecting a symbol helps identify what the symbol represents.

name: AGV removal is described as a high-risk action
description: The speaker identifies removing an AGV from an active system as one of the worst actions a user can take and explicitly says not to remove an AGV.

name: Container Selection screen supports tote and location lookup
description: The related training frame shows a Container Selection screen for totes and containers, including visual rack states and a way to find a tote by typing a location or number.

name: Container Selection color states for tote presence
description: The training frame associates color states on the Container Selection display with tote presence and rack emptiness.

name: Preferred customer-facing interfaces for removal actions
description: Customers should be directed to use AVEVA or the host/hospital interface rather than performing certain removals directly in Geek.

name: Orange station cells include workstation ID information
description: Orange cells represent stations, and selecting one shows additional station-related information including the workstation ID.

name: Charger Selection screen information
description: The Charger Selection view is used to select a charger by charger ID and inspect charger-related information including status and the robot currently associated with that charger.

name: Disabled charger status as a logical allocation control
description: Disabling a charger does not shut down the charger hardware; it logically marks the charging location as unavailable for AGV allocation.

name: OptiSweep-managed charging control and system interactions
description: Charging is handled within OptiSweep rather than by Geek, with callbacks and messages exchanged when chargers are disabled or enabled.

name: AGB low-battery red flashing indication
description: When an AGB battery level goes under 30%, the AGB will start flashing red.

name: Container Selection screen location-based tote lookup
description: The Container Selection screen supports finding a tote by entering a location number and selecting the rack or AGV where it is located, if it is in the system.

name: RMS section end marker in training session
description: The RMS section is ending during this training segment.

name: Aveva Walkthrough slide reference
description: A visible training frame shows the text "Aveva Walkthrough 32," serving as a slide or screen reference within the training material.

name: Session break discussion during training transition
description: The speakers discuss whether to take a break, indicating this segment is a training-session transition rather than an operational instruction segment.

name: AVEVA Walkthrough segment marker
description: This training video segment appears to be a title or transition slide labeled "Aveva Walkthrough 32" rather than a live OptiSweep application screen.

name: HMI question-and-answer discussion segment
description: This training video segment is identified as an HMI discussion or question-and-answer portion of the Day 1 training.

name: Low-legibility HMI video frame reference
description: A related training video frame is associated with the HMI discussion, but the frame content is not readable enough to extract stable operational details.

name: HMI identified as a training topic
description: The HMI is an active topic in Day 1 OptiSweep training and participant questions are directed toward it.

name: Viva main overview screen
description: The Viva main overview is presented as the home screen for overall system visibility and navigation.

name: Main menu and subscreen navigation on Viva overview
description: The overview screen includes a main menu used to navigate to multiple subscreens and related views.

name: System control actions shown on the Viva overview
description: The right-hand side of the Viva overview displays high-level system control actions including startup, shutdown, bag out, purge, resume, pause, and AGV-related controls.

name: System layout elements visible from the overview
description: The overview screen's system layout shows major material-handling areas and supports clicking icons for more information.

name: System bag out behavior
description: The bag out control system supports a system-wide bag out that closes destinations and exchanges occupied destinations or chutes containing parcels.

name: Bag out can be selected by sorter leg
description: The bag out control supports selecting a bag out by leg of the sorter rather than only as a full-system action.

name: Manual bag out includes cancel bag out capability
description: For manual bag out, Fortna provides a cancel bag out function that cancels exchange tasks that are not already in process.

name: Overall System AGV Status screen
description: A screen labeled Overall System AGV Status presents fleet-level AGV information in two sections.

name: Top section fields on Overall System AGV Status
description: The top section of the Overall System AGV Status view shows detailed information for all AGVs, including ID, status, destination, and errors.

name: Overall System AGV Status top section
Bottom section filtered to AGVs with errors
description: The bottom section of the Overall System AGV Status view is dedicated to AGVs with errors.

name: Overall System AGV Status bottom section
Overall System Bag Out Control
description: Overall system bag out is a control concept that closes destinations and exchanges totes containing parcels.
aliases: overall system bag out control system bag out

name: Pre Bag Out Exchange Scope
description: Pre bag out exchanges the lowest 25 percent of destinations per sorter leg.

name: Overall System AGV Status popup overview
description: An AGV status popup presents detailed information for AGVs in the overall system view.

name: AGV status popup information fields
description: The AGV status popup includes core fields used to summarize AGV state and issues.

name: Top section of Overall System AGV Status
Error-focused section of AGV status popup
description: The lower portion of the AGV status popup is reserved for AGVs with errors and provides additional detail for those cases.

name: Bottom section of Overall System AGV Status
Hot bin behavior in OptiSweep
description: Hot bins are bins associated with totes marked for hot bin handling, causing chute close and exchange behavior.

name: Hot bin disable effect on chute reopening
description: Hot bin disable does not reopen chutes after exchange is complete.

name: API page overview in Aveva
description: An Aveva page referred to as the API page exposes system-level OptiSweep functions through APIs and is shown on the left side of the system display.

name: System State display on the API page
description: The API page includes a System State field that shows the current state the system is in.

name: System Startup and AGV staging context
description: System Startup is described as the function that triggers OptiSweep to stage AGVs for exchanges after AGVs have been kept in a shutdown state between sorts to allow charging.

name: System Bag Out close-out concept
description: Close out, associated with System Bag Out, closes all chutes and exchanges totes with items at the end of a sort, with labels printed for totes with items.

name: System Shutdown state for AGV charger rotation
description: System Shutdown is described as the state the system should be put in when the sort is done so AGVs can rotate on the charger.

name: System Purge exchanges all totes without label printing
description: System Purge is described as a close-out-like function that exchanges all totes in the system and does not print a label at the tipper.

name: Overall System Aveva API page functions
description: The Overall System Aveva API page includes controls and pop-up links for metrics, tipper stats, bag out control, zone configuration, and current errors.

name: Reset Metrics behavior
description: Metrics are reset automatically when a new sort plan is loaded, and can also be manually reset from the Reset Metrics control.

name: Reset Tipper Stats control
description: The page includes a Reset Tipper Stats control, and the OCR text indicates tipper metrics are reset when a new sort plan is loaded but can also be manually reset.

name: Metrics and errors pop-up references
description: The page provides pop-up access to system metrics and current errors through Get metrics and Get errors.

name: Zone configuration page reference
description: The Overall System Aveva API page includes a Zone configuration option that opens the zone configuration page.

name: Aveva API incorporates selected Geek+ RMS AGV commands
description: Selected Geek+ RMS commands were implemented in the Aveva interface/API so users can perform certain AGV-related actions from Aveva.

name: Safety note about E-stop before restart
description: The speaker states that the system should be E-stopped before performing a restart.

name: AGV initialization popup on the tote side
description: The speaker states that on the tote side an operator can initialize an AGV through a popup interface.

name: System Metrics page for real-time item exchange KPIs
description: A System Metrics Aveva API page is shown as a real-time KPI view for tracking item exchanges.

name: Lane status values shown in the KPI view
description: The KPI page includes a status field with example values indicating whether a lane or tracked entity is active, bypassed, or not tracking.

name: status field on System Metrics page
Zone information displayed alongside KPI data
description: The KPI view includes zone information, and the training notes that each side can have multiple zones.

name: zone display on System Metrics page
Zone Config Aveva API page overview
description: The Zone Config Aveva API page is presented as an interface that provides an overview of lane assignments, their respective zones, and processing sequence numbers.

name: Get Zone Configuration function
description: The Get Zone Configuration function is described as fetching the current configuration of all lanes to provide visibility into how each lane is set up within the system.

name: Update Zone Configuration function
description: The Update Zone Configuration function is described as allowing users to modify zone settings to adapt operations based on system needs or changing requirements.

name: Tote task API functions
description: The displayed tote management API includes functions for retrieving the current tote task and resending a tote task command.

name: Tote exchange API functions
description: The displayed tote management API includes manual tote exchange functions by tote ID and by lane number, along with exchange settings retrieval.

name: Tote add and remove API functions
description: The displayed tote management API includes functions to add a specified tote to the system and remove a specified tote from the system.

name: Zone Config interface overview
description: The Zone Config Aveva API page is presented as an interface for viewing lane assignments, associated zones, and processing sequence numbers.

name: Initialize Tote Aveva API page overview
description: An Aveva API page is used to initialize a tote for processing in the system.

name: Initialize Tote input fields
description: The tote initialization interface uses BarcodeID, StationID, and ToteID as key input values.

name: Initialize Tote response behavior
description: The interface displays the result of the tote initialization request in a response field, including confirmation or error information.

name: AGV-related limitation for tote initialization
description: Tote initialization may be rejected when totes are on an AGV, and distinguishes this from AGVs not in the system or AGVs that have been removed.

name: Tote Task interface overview
description: The Tote Task interface provides visibility into tote movements within the warehouse.

name: Tote Task interface data fields
description: The Tote Task interface includes identifiers and task-related fields for tracking tote activity.

name: Exchange type and exchange readiness information
description: The Tote Task view includes exchange-related status information such as exchange type, priority, original destination, and readiness for exchange.

name: Tote Error field reference
description: The Tote Task interface includes a Tote Error field for tote-related error visibility.

name: Tote Exchange Settings interface overview
description: The Tote Exchange Settings interface is an Aveva API page used to view and manage parameters related to the tote exchange process.

name: Tote exchange threshold categories
description: The tote exchange settings include threshold categories for pickup, priority, and close, represented on the screen for both cube and count methods.

name: Tote exchange method options
description: The software supports tote exchange evaluation based on counts, cube, or a combination of cube and count.

name: Tote exchange weight-related parameters
description: The Tote Exchange Settings screen includes weight-related parameters labeled Maximum Weight and Weight Threshold.

name: Tote exchange settings update ownership and project finalization
description: Tote exchange settings can be updated by the customer, but are generally finalized with the project team and UPS at the end of UAT.

name: Aviva characterized primarily as an HMI interface
description: The training describes Aviva primarily as an HMI that shows service status and can issue some startup-related actions through APIs, but is not presented as the system that manages core logic.

name: Expectation that recurring issues should not repeat
description: The training discussion states that known issues should not continue happening repeatedly.

name: Overall System Statistics overview
description: An Overall System Statistics area contains Main Statistics and core system statistics.

name: E-stop statistics as a statistics type
description: E-stop is one of the statistics types available within the Overall System Statistics view.

name: Volume statistics categories
description: Volume is shown as a statistics type, with categories including Total Exchanges, To Tipper, and To Hospital.

name: Customer-defined calculations in the Overall System HMI
description: The Overall System HMI includes a customer-defined calculations area for metrics calculated by the customer.

name: Types of customer-defined calculations
description: There are three types of customer-defined calculations: system statistics, bin statistics, and tipper statistics.

name: Customer-requested origin of custom metrics
description: The training explains that the custom defined metrics were requested by UPS and developed in coordination with the team.

name: Overall System RMS screen
description: An Overall System RMS page is associated with the Geek+ RMS web page.

name: Thin-client visibility limits affect direct RMS viewing
description: FORTNA personnel cannot directly see RMS on thin clients and instead rely on API or database access to understand what is shown.

name: RMS page is referenced for remote availability
description: The capability being discussed is remotely available and directs viewers to the RMS page.

name: Overall System AGV Status page
description: An HMI page is titled "Overall System AGV Status."

name: Active AGV faults display on Overall System RMS
description: The Overall System RMS page includes a display area for active AGV faults on the right side of the page.

name: AUV status pop-up screen
description: An AUV status pop-up provides detailed status information.

name: Overall System AGV Status page
description: A page titled "Overall System AGV Status" is presented as showing current status information.

FORTNA OptiSweep Training Day 2
description: An introductory training video segment covers FORTNA OptiSweep Training - Day 2.

name: Morning Location Difference Note
description: The training opening slide notes that the morning location is different.

name: Training Video Recording Provenance
description: The recording date and named organizers or contributors are identified.

name: OptiSweep Technical Training Scope
description: This training segment identifies message flow, database, API, Ignition, and services as major technical areas covered in the OptiSweep training.

name: Message Flow, Database, and API Topics
description: The training contents identify message flow, database, and API as distinct technical areas within the OptiSweep training material.

name: Ignition and Services Topics
description: The training contents identify Ignition and services as technical areas covered in the OptiSweep training.

name: OptiSweep architecture overview
description: The training architecture shows OptiSweep software modules communicating with UPS equipment, PLCs, Ignition, Aveva HMI, SQL Server, and Geek+ robotics systems.

name: XLe chat communication module
description: The XLe chat communication module communicates with the XLe chat OBC communication module, which subscribes to tags in Ignition and supports reading and writing from the tippers.

name: Sorter Sweeper module
description: The Sorter Sweeper module is described as a tote state machine that tracks package and tote information from arrival through the tipper.

name: Robotics and Geek+ communication integration
description: The Robotics module processes tote movement requests using maps, while the Geek+ communication module translates robotics commands into Geek+ API requests.

name: Ignition and Aveva HMI data layer
description: Ignition is described as the HMI base used to collect data and send it to the Aveva HMI for UPS operations.

name: Sorter Sweeper module architecture and responsibilities
description: The Sorter Sweeper module orchestrates tote movement and functions as the tote state machine.

name: Sorter Robotics module and AGV task interface
description: The Sorter Robotics module acts as the state machine for AGVs and converts tote tasks into commands for Geek Plus execution.

name: OPC COM module and tag communication
description: The OPC COM module provides tag-based communication between OptiSweep components, the OPC server, and connected equipment.

name: XLE COM and UPS Chat communication
description: The XLE COM module manages communication between Sorter Sweeper and the UPS Chat server.

name: UPS sorter data and tote destination concepts
description: The UPS interface exchanges parcel scan attributes, destination information, tote status messages, and label data associated with sorter operations.

name: Database Walkthrough
description: The segment is titled "Database Walkthrough."

name: Robotics Module as the AGV State Machine
description: The Robotics module acts as the state machine for automated guided vehicles (AGVs) within the OptiSweep design.

name: Robotics Module AGV Command Vocabulary
description: The Robotics module generates AGV commands associated with tote handling, movement, cancellation, and charging.

name: Geek+ Communication Module
description: The system design includes a Geek+ communication module associated with executing Robotics module commands for AGVs.

name: Database Tables
description: Database tables are the subject of the database walkthrough introduced in this training segment.

name: OptiSweep database architecture overview
description: OptiSweep operates within a Fortna WCS environment that includes WCS data containers, entity logs, and PLC communication, along with OptiSweep-related databases and SQL jobs.

name: WCS EntityLogs and DeveloperLogs
description: OptiSweep uses the WCS EntityLogs database for application logging and debugging information.

name: Audit and Geek AGV task logging
description: The Audit and Geek AGV databases preserve identifiers, command history, and task history associated with robotics and Geek Plus operations.

name: Lattice codes and station identifiers
description: The lattice code model stores lattice codes associated with station IDs and supports conversion between robotics station identifiers and the location identifiers required by Geek.

name: OPC connection configuration and subscribed tags
description: OPC Comms stores the connection parameters and OPC tag information used by the software bridge to communicate with OPC.

name: Robot Location database model
description: The Robot Location database model contains location attributes used to describe stations and other locations in the system.

name: Location types and location status terminology
description: The training presents location-type terminology for sorter, tipper, hospital, GLD, and shutdown-related locations.

name: Sorter Side database model
description: The Sorter Side database model defines sorter-side identifiers, entrance and exit queue locations, tipper count, and disabled state.

name: Sorter-side tipper distribution concept
description: The training describes tipper count and round-robin or closest-tipper selection as concepts used to distribute sorter-side volume across tippers.

name: Location zones, cell codes, and coordinates
description: The training distinguishes zones, cell codes, and location XY coordinates as location-related data concepts.

name: Robotics Database Overview
description: The training material presents a Robotics Database and a Hospital Database Model as collections of related operational data entities.

name: Robot, Command, and Activity Data Entities
description: The database overview includes entities for robots, robot commands, command activity, robot locations, and robot task activity.

name: Charging, Error, Task, Tote, and Sorter Data Entities
description: The database overview includes data entities for charging thresholds and activity, system errors, tasks, totes, stations, sorters, and related operational records.

name: Sorter-side and tipper-arm association
description: Sorter sides are associated with nearby tipper arms and operator stations through configured mapping.

name: Sorter-side enablement and configuration
description: Sorter-side enablement is represented in the configuration data and can differ by implementation phase.

name: Sort locations database model
description: The sort locations database model records sorted locations, associated queue locations, sorter-side associations, and queue sequence.

name: Shutdown staging database model
description: The shutdown staging table maps AGV staging locations for shutdown states based on whether an AGV is carrying a tote.

name: Sorter zone exit queue sequence mapping
description: A mapping file associates sorter zone sequence numbers with sorter locations or stations.

name: Sorter queue and array sequence concept
description: The training distinguishes the sorter exit queue from its underlying queue or array sequence representation.
aliases: sorter zone exit queue sequence ID

name: AGV ordering during sorter queue compression
description: Sorter queue compression preserves the relative sequence of AGVs associated with the same destination zone.

name: RMS Map Monitor emergency-stop status
description: The captured RMS Map Monitor screen displays robot and system emergency-stop information.

name: Charging database model tables
description: OptiSweep charging configuration is represented through separate database model tables for charging areas, charging locations, and charging thresholds.

name: Charging area configuration
description: A charging area represents a separate charging region with configured entrance and exit locations and a disabled status.

name: Charging location and tote-stand mapping
description: Charging location records identify individual chargers, their stations, associated tote stands, charging-area associations, and disabled status.

name: Charging threshold values
description: Charging threshold records contain values used by OptiSweep application code to determine charging-related states.

name: Sorter-side charger assignment
description: Chargers are associated with sorter-side identifiers, and charging behavior uses assigned chargers with cross-side availability described for emergency cases.

name: Robot Command Database active-command tracking
description: The Robot Command Database model table tracks active robot commands requested by the Robotics module for AGVs.

name: Vendor-agnostic robot command model
description: OptiSweep represents robot commands in a generic internal format rather than a vendor-specific command format.

name: Robot Command Activity historical records
description: Robot Command Activity stores historical records for completed or otherwise finalized robot commands.

name: Robot location and queue capacity concepts
description: Robot location data includes current and destination locations, while location capacity limits the number of AGVs permitted at certain queues or stations.

name: AGV charging control responsibility
description: In the described OptiSweep configuration, WCS manages assignment of AGVs to chargers, while the RMS charging control is modified or unavailable for that assignment.

name: Robot Task Current and Archived Records
description: The Robot Task database model tracks the status of tote tasks requested by the Sorter Sweeper module. Completed tasks are archived to Robot Task Activity.

name: AGV Error Reference Model
description: The AGV Error model table stores error codes and descriptions and classifies errors as critical or non-critical for metric purposes.

name: AGV Active Error and Error Activity Records
description: The AGV Active Error Database model records AGV errors currently in the system, while resolved or removed errors are archived to AGV Error Activity.

name: Location Dwell Current and Archived Records
description: The Location Active Dwell model table displays active dwell records at sort locations marked for dwell tracking. Completed dwell records are archived to Location Dwell Activity.

name: Location Active Dwell Model
description: The Robotics Database includes a LocationActiveDwellModel table that displays active AGV dwell records at locations marked for DwellTracking.

name: Location Dwell Activity Archive
description: Completed location dwell records are archived in LocationDwellActivity after an AGV leaves the tracked location.

name: Operational Dwell Metrics
description: The training describes dwell time as an operational statistic used to understand waiting, idle time, and potential bottlenecks at locations such as hospitals and tippers.

name: System Error Definition table
description: The System Error Definition table stores the definitions of system errors.

name: System Database Model
description: The SystemDatabaseModel represents the configuration and current state of the robotics system.

name: System Database Model Fields
description: The displayed SystemDatabaseModel record includes entity timestamps, status, and sort identification fields.

name: Robotics Database Model Tables
description: The robotics database contains system, robot, task, location, charging, error, and sorter-related database models.

name: Sorter Sweeper Database Overview
description: A training slide presents the Sorter Sweeper Database and lists data fields associated with sorter operations, destinations, packages, totes, stations, lanes, robots, and related system activity.

name: Sorter, Lane, and Tipper Database Fields
description: The database overview includes fields referencing sorters, sorter sides, lanes, tippers, and associated statuses or identifiers.

name: Package, Tote, and Destination Database Fields
description: The database overview lists fields for package identification, tote information, destination data, sorting, and package classification.

name: OptiSweep robotics database landscape
description: The robotics database environment consists of multiple databases rather than a single system database.

name: SystemDatabaseModel configuration and sort state
description: The SystemDatabaseModel is presented as showing the system configuration and the current sort GUID.

name: Sorter database model overview
description: The sorter database model is an overview of storage data, relationships, configuration, activities, and foreign-key connections.

name: Sorter interface identifiers
description: The sorter model includes an XLE IP address and an XLE name used to identify the receiver when messages are sent to the sorter.

name: Sorter location model and location types
description: The sorter location model represents stations on the map and includes sorter, tipper, hospital, and induction location types.

name: AGV location presence notifications
description: The sorter model uses AGV-reported cell codes in relation to induction and hospital locations, and the system notifies the associated hospital controller when an AGV is present.

name: Sorter location attributes and lane status
description: Sorter locations have attributes for sorter name, sorter side, zone, sequence, lane, lane delay, lane status, destinations, and tipper-related configuration.

name: Hospital tags model
description: The hospital tags model processes data from the hospital controller and maintains tag definitions used to communicate with PLC-connected equipment and displays.

name: Tag variable types and value storage
description: Hospital tag records support different tag data types through a variable type and associated value fields.

name: Configuration tables as software behavior settings
description: Several database tables serve as modular configuration that tells the software how to read and write data and how to interpret equipment settings.

name: Hospital pickup and drop-off location identifiers
description: Hospital station pickup and drop-off identifiers are associated with location identifiers in the location table.

name: Tipper station reference
description: Tipper stations represent operator stations and include standard and GLD station types.

name: Tag Read and Tag Write Logs
description: The tag read and tag write logs record tags that the system reads and writes.

name: Tipper Departure Activity Model Records
description: Tipper Departure Activity Model records capture activity when an AGV is sent away from a tipper or drop-off location.

name: Tipper Departure Record Fields
